findings.finding_text: Attrition liability triggers at 75% pickup rather than the 70% threshold CD standardizes on, and the damages rate is set at 75% of ADR rather than 70%. Both the trigger and the rate are stricter against Group than CD's position.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition should be measured cumulatively with liability triggered only if pickup falls below 70% of the block, with damages calculated at 70% of the confirmed group room rate.
findings.proposed_language: If Group fails to occupy at least seventy percent (70%) of the room block reserved for the Event, Hotel shall assess attrition damages against Group. The attrition liability rate shall be seventy percent (70%) of the average daily room rate applicable to the block, multiplied by the number of unoccupied room nights representing the shortfall below the 70% threshold.
findings.quoted_text: If Group fails to occupy at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the room block reserved for the Event, Hotel shall assess attrition damages against Group in accordance with the provisions of this clause.
findings.exposure_basis: Difference between 75% and 70% thresholds equals 5% of 210 rooms x 4 nights = 42 room nights; plus rate differential of 5% of $419 ADR applied to shortfall nights below threshold. Approximate combined exposure calculated on 210-room block at $419 ADR across 4 nights.

findings.finding_text: The cutoff/rooming list deadline is set at 32 days prior to arrival, which exceeds CD's 21-30 day standard window, giving attendees less time to book at the group rate.
findings.cd_standard: The room block cutoff date should be no earlier than 21-30 days prior to arrival, with post-cutoff reservations available at the group rate subject to availability.
findings.proposed_language: Group shall provide the Hotel with a final rooming list containing all guest names, room type preferences, and arrival and departure dates no later than twenty-one (21) days prior to the Event's opening day.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall provide the Hotel with a final rooming list containing all guest names, room type preferences, and arrival and departure dates no later than thirty-two (32) days prior to the Event's opening day.

findings.finding_text: Post-cutoff reservations are only offered at group rate subject to Hotel's yield management practices and market conditions, with an explicit statement that the Hotel's primary obligation is to maximize occupancy and revenue rather than honor the group rate — this undercuts the availability-at-group-rate commitment CD requires.
findings.cd_standard: After the cutoff date, the hotel should continue to accept reservations at the group rate on a space-available basis, not subject to yield-management repricing.
findings.proposed_language: After the cutoff date, Hotel will continue to accept reservations at the group rate on a space-available basis, without repricing based on yield management practices or market conditions.
findings.quoted_text: Pricing and room type availability following the cutoff shall be determined solely by Hotel's yield management practices and current market conditions.

findings.finding_text: Menu pricing is locked 14 months prior to the event, exceeding CD's 12-month maximum. Additionally, the shortfall penalty is set at 40% of the difference rather than CD's 35%, and the Hotel reserves unilateral discretion to negotiate or waive the shortfall, which is one-sided but not itself a deviation against Group (noted for completeness, the 40% rate and 14-month lock are the deviations).
findings.cd_standard: F&B minimums should lock menu pricing no earlier than 12 months before the event, and shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall provide Group with a menu and pricing proposal no earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event date. Should Group's actual Food and Beverage expenditures fall short of the Minimum Commitment, Group shall pay thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual charges and the Minimum Commitment.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide Group with a menu and pricing proposal at least fourteen (14) months prior to the Event date, and all menu selections and per-person pricing shall be locked and shall not be subject to increase or modification after that date.

findings.finding_text: The complimentary room ratio is set at one room per 45 occupied room nights, which is less favorable to Group than CD's standard ratio of one per 40.
findings.cd_standard: Complimentary rooms should be earned at a ratio of one complimentary room for every 40 occupied, revenue-producing room nights.
findings.proposed_language: Group will receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) occupied, revenue-producing room nights actualized, calculated cumulatively across the entire room block.
findings.quoted_text: The complimentary room ratio is forty-five (45), meaning that for every forty-five (45) paid room nights generated by Group, the Hotel shall provide one (1) complimentary room night at no charge to Group.

findings.finding_text: The monthly finance charge on overdue undisputed balances is set at 1.3%, exceeding CD's 1% (or legal maximum, if lower) cap. Additionally, the dispute window for invoice charges is only 12 days, shorter than the 30-day review period CD's standard calls for, and the prepayment requirement absent credit approval is set at 75% with no defined cap language beyond that figure (this last point is consistent with the 'defined percentage' requirement, so not a separate finding).
findings.cd_standard: Finance charges on undisputed late balances should be capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less, with a 30-day dispute window before any finance charge accrues.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall assess a monthly finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%), or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, on any portion of an undisputed invoice balance remaining unpaid thirty (30) days after the invoice due date. Group shall have thirty (30) days from receipt of invoice to dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount.
findings.quoted_text: The Monarch shall assess a monthly finance charge of 1.3% on any portion of an undisputed invoice balance remaining unpaid thirty (30) days after the invoice due date.

findings.finding_text: The invoice dispute window is only twelve (12) days, shorter than CD's standard 30-day window, after which disputes are deemed waived.
findings.cd_standard: Group should have 30 days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to review and dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount.
findings.proposed_language: Any invoice dispute must be submitted in writing to The Monarch's Accounting Department within thirty (30) days of invoice receipt; disputes submitted after such period shall be deemed waived.
findings.quoted_text: Any invoice dispute must be submitted in writing to The Monarch's Accounting Department within twelve (12) days of invoice receipt; disputes submitted after such period shall be deemed waived.

findings.finding_text: The clause states that commission and pickup credits will be calculated only on Group's original contracted rate and will not be adjusted upward when the rate parity provision lowers Group's actual room revenue — meaning the retroactive rate-matching reduces Group's billed revenue without a corresponding reduction to what counts toward pickup/attrition credit favorability, but more importantly it fixes commission/credit calculation to the original (higher) rate even though CD's standard ties commission and pickup credit protection to the adjusted matching outcome without singling out this asymmetric carve-out; the provision as drafted freezes commission/rebate calculations to original rate regardless of adjustment, which is favorable on commission but the overall rate parity 'absolute and without exception' framing combined with retroactive adjustment mechanics otherwise matches CD's ask. The deviation is that commission/pickup credit is explicitly walled off from any retroactive adjustment in a way that is not clearly required to remain fully commissionable and creditable as CD's standard specifies for the adjusted rooms.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel sells below the group rate, Group's rate should be adjusted to match, including retroactively, without losing commission or pickup credit — meaning commission/pickup credit should reflect full value regardless of rate adjustment direction.
findings.proposed_language: Any rooms subject to a retroactive rate adjustment under this clause shall remain fully commissionable and creditable toward Group's pickup, complimentary-room credits, and any attrition calculation, calculated without reduction resulting from the rate adjustment.
findings.quoted_text: Commission and pickup credits shall be computed on Group's original contracted rate, and any reduction in Group's billed room revenue shall not proportionally reduce the commission or credit owed to Group.

findings.finding_text: The clause requires costs of auxiliary aids to be divided between Group and Hotel via negotiation, rather than clearly allocating Group's funding responsibility to aids in its own function space and the Hotel's responsibility for aids in guest rooms/common areas as CD's standard specifies.
findings.cd_standard: Costs of auxiliary aids should be divided by responsibility: Group funds aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel funds aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas — not an open-ended negotiated split.
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Both parties will communicate known auxiliary-aid and accessible-guest-room needs to the other in advance.
findings.quoted_text: the cost of such auxiliary aids shall be divided between the Group and the Hotel...and the parties shall negotiate in good faith to determine the appropriate allocation of costs for each specific auxiliary aid, with the Hotel bearing its proportionate share of expenses reasonably attributable to the Hotel's facilities or obligations under the Americans with Disabilities Act.

findings.finding_text: The Group's termination right is conditioned on demonstrating in good faith that the change materially affects Hotel's performance or alters service standards — an added burden of proof not contemplated by CD's standard, which allows termination at Group's discretion within the notice window.
findings.cd_standard: Group may, at its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving notice of a change in ownership, management, or brand.
findings.proposed_language: Upon receipt of notice of a change in brand, management, or ownership, the Group may, at its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement without penalty or liability within thirty (30) days of such notice.
findings.quoted_text: The Group's termination right shall be conditioned upon the Group demonstrating, in good faith, that the change materially affects the Hotel's ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement or materially alters the character or service standards of the property.

findings.finding_text: The termination window given to Group is only 25 days from notice, shorter than the 30-day window CD's standard calls for.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of receiving notice of a change in ownership, management, or brand.
findings.proposed_language: Upon receipt of notice of a change in brand, management, or ownership, the Group shall have the right to terminate this Agreement without penalty or liability within thirty (30) days of such notice.
findings.quoted_text: Upon receipt of notice of a change in brand, management, or ownership, the Group shall have the right to terminate this Agreement without penalty or liability within twenty-five (25) days of such notice, provided that the Group's election to terminate is exercised by written notice delivered to the Hotel.

findings.finding_text: The venue clause designates the state and federal courts located in the state where Group maintains its principal offices, but does not specify the city where Group is located as CD's standard requires for the actual dispute venue, leaving the specific court location broader than CD's position (state-wide rather than Group's home city).
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and dispute venue should be the state and city where the group is located.
findings.proposed_language: This Agreement will be construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the state in which Group is located. Any unresolved controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement will be settled by a court of law in the city in which Group is located.
findings.quoted_text: The parties irrevocably submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in such state for the resolution of any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the parties' performance hereunder.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel's advance notice of collective bargaining agreement expirations is only 9 months, short of CD's one-year (or specified date) standard.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should give a year's advance notice of when its collective bargaining agreements expire.
findings.proposed_language: One year in advance, the Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide written notice to the Group of any expiration, non-renewal, or material breach in any collective bargaining agreement, union contract, or labor agreement covering employees at the Hotel no later than nine (9) months prior to the expiration date of such agreement.

findings.finding_text: Group's cancellation right for a labor dispute is limited to a 75-day window after becoming aware of the action, rather than the 90-day proximity-to-event trigger and unconditional right CD's standard specifies (CD ties the right to disputes arising within 90 days of the event, not a 75-day awareness window), narrowing Group's protection window.
findings.cd_standard: If a strike, lockout, or expired contract with union employees arises within 90 days of the event, the group should be able to cancel with no liability, regardless of whether the hotel can technically still perform.
findings.proposed_language: If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, picketing occurs, or a strike or lockout occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability, regardless of whether Hotel is able to perform.
findings.quoted_text: the Group shall have the right to cancel this Agreement without liability, penalty, or forfeiture of any payments or deposits within seventy-five (75) days of becoming aware of such labor dispute or action.

findings.finding_text: Although outside vendors are permitted, the clause imposes an outside vendor surcharge, listed as $0.00 in this instance but structurally present as a mandatory fee mechanism, and the Group's exclusivity extends only to AV, decorating, security, and transportation, not the full list (e.g., floral) CD's standard calls for. The presence of a named surcharge line item (even at zero) signals the Hotel reserves the contractual right to impose one, which is a deviation from CD's no-fee standard on principle, and the omission of floral vendors from the enumerated categories is a gap versus CD's full list.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use the outside vendor of its choice — including floral — at no additional fee or surcharge, without a surcharge mechanism reserved in the contract.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services or rentals including but not limited to audio-visual, exhibit decorating, security, floral, transportation, and tours. No outside vendor surcharge shall apply to Group's engagement of outside vendors.
findings.quoted_text: the Group shall remit to the Hotel an outside vendor surcharge in the amount of "$0.00". This surcharge shall be payable in full upon execution of this Agreement and represents the Hotel's sole additional compensation for the privilege of hosting outside vendors on the Hotel's premises during the Event.

findings.finding_text: The contract states no deposit is charged, but includes language referencing 'any security deposit or other funds held by the Hotel' without ever establishing a defined refund window matching CD's 30-day standard tied to itemized documented damage — the 30-day refund reference applies only in the no-damage scenario, and there is no explicit provision addressing timing when a deposit does exist beyond the damage-triggered scenario, leaving the deposit refund mechanism incompletely specified relative to CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Any security or damage deposit should be refundable within a defined 30-day window absent documented, itemized damage, and should not be commingled with unrelated charges.
findings.proposed_language: Any security deposit collected under this Agreement will be refunded in full within thirty (30) days of the event's conclusion unless the Hotel provides Group with an itemized accounting of specific, documented damage caused by Group or its attendees beyond normal wear and tear. The deposit may not be applied toward attrition, cancellation, or F&B minimum shortfalls.
findings.quoted_text: Following such payment or within thirty (30) days of Group's departure should no damage occur, any remaining deposit shall be refunded to the billing contact on Group's master account.

analysis.document_notes: The contract is a fairly comprehensive, well-drafted Group Sales Agreement that already incorporates many CD-favorable provisions (cumulative attrition with 95% occupancy credit, resale mitigation duty, walk/relocation credit, force majeure including pandemics and travel advisories, named storm clause, termination for cause independent of cancellation damages, ADA warranty, attendee data protection, ADA-style ratio credit protections for comp rooms surviving attrition, ADA ratio ambiguity aside). Several numeric thresholds (attrition trigger/rate, cutoff days, F&B lock-in period and shortfall %, comp room ratio, finance charge rate, dispute window, labor notice periods, brand-change window) are set at values that differ from CD's specific benchmarks, sometimes narrowly. No illegible or structurally unusual pages were encountered; Schedule A referenced in the cancellation clause was reproduced as a table within the text and reviewed as part of the cancellation clause. The outside vendor surcharge is nominally $0.00 in this instance, but the presence of a surcharge mechanism at all is flagged since CD's standard rejects any surcharge structure, not just a nonzero one.
